title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier‑Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared‑Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study (study‑cnd‑2026‑001) to assess whether a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increases oracle pass rates for LLM‑produced network configurations on vendor‑diverse emulated NetOps intent→configuration tasks. The frozen design used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (one generator call per pair consumed by both conditions), declared model gpt‑5‑mini, a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a repair budget ≤1 call/task. Execution produced 200 complete pairs (400 episodes), model_calls_used=200, and repair calls invoked=0. Results: baseline = 200/200 oracle passes; guarded = 200/200 oracle passes; absolute paired difference = 0.00 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00], bootstrap_resamples=10000, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p=1.00. The null result is design‑bound: every shared candidate passed the deterministic oracle, so the repair stage was never exercised. We release the full audited artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and SHA‑256 digests) and provide artifact‑anchored recommendations for informative follow‑ups (independent generation semantics, calibrated difficulty, larger repair budgets, validator stress tests).

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs are increasingly explored as intent→configuration agents for network operations. Practical deployment demands operationally correct outputs (ordering, safety, vendor idiom compliance), yet LLMs can produce plausible but unsafe configurations. A common system design to mitigate misconfiguration is generate→validate→repair: a generator proposes a candidate, a deterministic validator (oracle) checks objective properties (reachability, protected interfaces, transient‑state safety), and, if the validator fails, a repair module attempts corrective generation. Published systems report improvements when validators constrain generation or when repairs exploit verifier counterexamples; however, rigorous preregistered comparisons with full artifact archives are scarce.

We preregistered study‑cnd‑2026‑001 to provide a confirmatory, fully archived measurement of whether verifier assistance increases oracle pass rates. The crucial preregistered design choice was generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate: one generator call per paired test produced a single candidate that both baseline (unconstrained) and guarded (verifier‑assisted) conditions consumed. That choice is central to the observed outcome and is reported, archived, and hashed in the execution bundle (see provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 1872df1e...). Our principal contribution is an artifact‑anchored account of the preregistered run, deterministic reconciliation of per‑file hashes and manifests, precise statistical reporting of the confirmatory test, and concrete artifact‑grounded guidance for informative experiment variants that avoid the ceiling effect documented here.
sections.related_work: Recent NetOps work spans intent translation, configuration synthesis, verifier/constraint augmentation, and repair workflows. Representative verified sources from the supplied evidence bundle include MeshAgent (constraint‑guided generation), NetConfEval (intent→configuration benchmarks), and verifier‑grounded program repair workflows (StruSpec). Those works motivate verifier‑assisted architectures and informed our preregistration (see cited_record_ids). Unlike many prior studies, we preregistered the estimand, generation semantics, validator, and analysis executor, executed the run autonomously, and archived every raw and derived artifact with SHA‑256 digests to permit reproducible audit (execution/execution_manifest.json; analysis/* artifacts). This manuscript situates the run against that prior art while emphasizing the methodological transparency required for operational claims.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design: The experiment was preregistered as study‑cnd‑2026‑001 (SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b1bb7...), which froze: primary_estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; declared_model = gpt‑5‑mini; validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; paired design with Npairs=200 (planned episodes=400). The preregistration also fixed statistical analysis (paired_binary_analysis_v1: paired bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples, seed=1729, and exact McNemar two‑sided test). All preregistration fields, including the sampling plan, exclusion rules, and stopping rules, are archived in the preregistration artifact referenced in the execution manifest.

Task bank and stratification (archived manifest): The preregistered task bank comprised 200 paired tasks stratified by protocol and vendor: four protocol buckets (BGP/OSPF/ACL/VLAN = 50 pairs each) with per‑protocol vendor allocation Cisco=17, Juniper=17, Arista=16 (total Cisco=68, Juniper=68, Arista=64). Complexity split: simple=100, complex=100. Each task entry in execution/task_manifest.jsonl includes intent text, initial and expected final states, required_sequence, constraints, and a reference_answer (see representative tasks e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001‑baseline.json; SHA‑256 eaf96a...). The manifest entries provide deterministic seeds and contamination checks used during generation.

Model, adapter, and generation semantics: The declared generator was gpt‑5‑mini via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model configuration is archived at execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 1acce925...). The frozen generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate) meant the system made exactly one generator call per pair and supplied the identical generated candidate to both the baseline and guarded scorers. This policy reduced model calls (model_calls_used=200) and directly constrained the trial structure; the execution manifest records these counts and per‑call provider traces (execution/provider_calls/*).

Validator, repair, and scoring: We used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scorer id recorded in every scoring artifact). The validator performs a deterministic syntactic+semantic parse of candidate configurations, simulates the intended configuration change against an emulated deterministic network model, and returns a normalized_configuration, valid boolean, parsed_command_count, violation list, and a validator trace. Repair was permitted but in this run repair_calls_invoked=0 (repair_applied=false in every validator trace); the repair budget ceiling (≤1 call/task) is preregistered.

Execution, logging and immutability: The autonomous run archived every raw response, provider trace, validator trace, and scoring file under execution/, and recorded a SHA‑256 digest per file in execution/execution_manifest.json. Deterministic_reconciliation checks (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) confirm per‑artifact accounting consistency. The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 consumed the per‑pair scoring JSON files and produced analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv) with SHA‑256 digests preserved.
sections.results:
Execution summary and raw outcomes (artifact‑backed): The run completed per preregistration: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200. Scoring summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4...): baseline_success_count = 200/200 (100%); guarded_success_count = 200/200 (100%). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...) is n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0.

Confirmatory inference (artifact: analysis/results.json): paired estimate = 0.00; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00] (bootstrap_resamples=10000, seed=1729). McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. These numbers and exact files are present in analysis/results.json and the analysis log (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = 940b48e7...).

Representative validator traces and exemplar pairs: Representative scoring and validator traces are archived; e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 eaf96aec...) shows the normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count=4, final_state dictionary, valid=true, and repair_applied=false. Similar condition‑matched artifacts exist for many pairs (execution/scoring/task-00000X‑{baseline,guarded}.json) and are listed in execution/execution_manifest.json with per‑file SHA‑256 digests.

Deterministic reconciliation: analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA‑256 799b23b9...) confirms internal accounting: complete_pair_count=200; baseline_from_contingency=200; guarded_from_contingency=200; hosted_model_call_event_count=200; cache_hit_count=0; cache_miss_count=200; all deterministic consistency checks passed. The reconciliation artifact enumerates per‑stage counts and verifies that every scoring record maps to a stored raw response and provider trace.
sections.discussion:
Why the null result occurred (design causal chain): The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics forced one generator call per pair; because each shared candidate passed the deterministic validator in every pair, the repair stage was never invoked (repair_calls_invoked = 0 across execution/responses/ and execution/scoring/ artifacts). Thus the guarded condition had no opportunity to improve on the baseline: empirically both conditions consumed identical passing artifacts, producing n11=200. This is a ceiling effect produced by a preregistered design choice (artifact: preregistration and execution/execution_manifest.json). The run therefore answers the preregistered estimand under the frozen design but does not measure verifier benefit in regimes where repairs can act.

Statistical interpretation and degenerate inference: Perfect concordance (all pairs passing) yields zero empirical variance for the paired difference; the bootstrap CI degenerates to the point mass [0.00,0.00], and exact McNemar reflects no discordant pairs (p=1.00). These are correct inferential consequences of the observed contingency (analysis artifacts). They do not imply the repair architecture is useless in general—only that under the frozen shared generation semantics and given the chosen task bank and generator behavior, repairs were not exercised.

Operational implications and artifact‑anchored recommendations: The artifact bundle permits exact replication and two concrete, low‑risk follow‑ups that will permit the repair module to act and reveal potential benefits: (1) independent generation semantics (generate one candidate per condition per pair) — this change converts the paired design into a fair within‑pair contrast of generator variability and allows repairs to act when baseline candidates fail; (2) calibrated task difficulty and adversarialization — extend execution/task_manifest.jsonl with higher‑difficulty tasks or boundary conditions so that some initial candidates fail the validator. Both variants are reproducible using the archived prompts and task manifest as seeds. Additional options include increasing the repair budget (>1), allowing iterative repair loops, and running across multiple generator models (multi‑model replication) to test generality. All of these variant experiment plans are supported by the existing artifacts and manifest structure and can be executed under the same adapter family (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) while preserving per‑file hashing for audit.

Threats to validity (artifact‑grounded): Internal validity — prompt sensitivity and generation semantics are the decisive design levers; we preserved the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and therefore observed the ceiling effect. Construct validity — the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces objective, emulation‑based oracles (reachability, protected interfaces, required sequence); oracle blind spots remain possible and are flagged by oracle_coverage diagnostics in per‑pair validator traces (execution/scoring/* entries include parser evidence and violation lists). External validity — single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic/emulated tasks limit generalization to other models, richer production images, or nondeterministic device behavior. Conclusion validity — the paired design was faithfully executed; inference is exact for the frozen estimand but the observed outcome is degenerate (no discordant pairs) because the guarded repair stage was not invoked.

Reproducibility and auditability (how to rerun or extend exactly): Every artifact required to rerun or extend the experiment is archived and SHA‑256 hashed in execution/execution_manifest.json. Key paths: preregistration (preregistration artifact recorded in execution manifest), initial master prompt provenance at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e...), per‑pair task manifest execution/task_manifest.jsonl, raw responses execution/responses/*.txt, provider traces execution/provider_calls/*.json, scoring/executor traces execution/scoring/*.json, analysis artifacts analysis/*.csv and analysis/results.json. Deterministic_reconciliation.json documents consistency checks and provider call counts. To run an independent‑generation variant, change generation_semantics to independent_per_condition in a new preregistration, update planned model calls accordingly (expected ≈400 generator calls), and rerun using the same adapter; the execution framework will archive the new provider calls and generate matching SHA‑256 digests for audit.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed an auditable paired emulation test of verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Both baseline and guarded conditions achieved 200/200 oracle passes; repairs were never invoked; paired difference=0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p=1.00). The null outcome is explained by the preregistered generation semantics and corresponding ceiling effect: a single shared candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle in every case. This run demonstrates the necessity of matching generation semantics and task difficulty to the scientific estimand: to measure repair effectiveness the pipeline must allow generator variance and oracle failures. We publish the full artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 digests) to enable reproducible follow‑ups that address the ceiling effect (independent generation, higher difficulty tasks, larger repair budgets, validator stress testing). All archived artifacts referenced above are included in the supplied bundle and hash manifest for audit.

limitations: Confirmatory conclusions apply only to the exact preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, single declared model gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, synthetic/emulated task bank of 200).

Shared_initial_candidate execution semantics created a ceiling effect: because the single shared generated candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle for every task, the guarded repair stage was never invoked (repair calls invoked = 0), preventing measurable guarded benefit in this run.
Emulation with a deterministic validator and synthetic tasks does not capture full production heterogeneity (real vendor images, runtime nondeterminism, device‑specific quirks).
Single‑model execution limits generality across model families and instruction‑tuning variants.
Repair budget was intentionally limited (≤1 call/task) by preregistration; richer iterative repair policies remain unexplored in this run.
Oracle blind spots (uncovered semantic failure modes) remain possible; oracle‑coverage diagnostics are archived and annotated in the artifact bundle.
